title: De Baptismo
author: Augustine

passages.original: \'Cyprianus\', inquiunt, \'cuius tantum meritum nouimus tantamque doctrinam, cum multis coepiscopis suis sententias proprias conferentibus in concilio statuit haereticos uel schismaticos, id est omnes qui extra unius ecclesiae communionem sunt, baptismum non habere, et ideo quisquis ab eis baptizatus ad ecclesiam uenerit esse in ecclesia baptizandum.\' non me terret auctoritas Cypriani, quia reficit humilitas Cypriani. magnum quidem meritum nouimus Cypriani episcopi et martyris, sed numquid maius quam Petri apostoli et martyris? de quo idem Cyprianus in epistula ad Quintum ita loquitur: nam nec Petrus, inquit, quem primum dominus elegit et super quem aedificauit ecclesiam suam, cum secum Paulus de circumcisione postmodum disoeptaret, uindicauit sibi aliquid insolenter aut arroganter adsumpsit, ut diceret se primatum tenere et obtemperari a nouellis et posteris sibi potius oportere, nec despexit Paulum quod ecclesiae prius persecutor fuisset, sed consilium ueritatis admisit et rationi legitimae quam Paulus uindicabat facile consensit, documentum scilicet nobis et concordiae et patientiae tribuens, ut non pertinaciter nostra amemus, sed quae aliquando a fratribus et collegis nostris utiliter et salubriter suggeruntur, si sint uera et legitima, ipsa potius nostra dicamus.
passages.english: "Cyprian," they say, "whose great merit and great learning we know, together with many of his fellow bishops contributing their own opinions, decreed in council that heretics or schismatics, that is, all who are outside the communion of the one church, do not have baptism, and that therefore whoever has been baptized by them and comes to the church must be baptized in the church." The authority of Cyprian does not frighten me, because the humility of Cyprian restores me. We do indeed know the great merit of Cyprian, bishop and martyr, but is it greater than that of Peter, apostle and martyr? Of him this same Cyprian speaks thus in his letter to Quintus: "For not even Peter," he says, "whom the Lord chose first and on whom he built his church, when Paul later disputed with him about circumcision, claimed anything for himself insolently or assumed anything arrogantly, so as to say that he held the primacy and that he ought rather to be obeyed by newcomers and those who came after; nor did he despise Paul because he had previously been a persecutor of the church, but he accepted the counsel of truth and readily agreed to the legitimate reasoning that Paul was maintaining, giving us, that is, an example both of concord and of patience, so that we should not obstinately love our own [views], but should rather count as our own those things which are at times usefully and wholesomely suggested by our brothers and colleagues, if they are true and legitimate."
passages.notes: "disoeptaret" read as "disceptaret" (disputed).

passages.original: qui cum crederent haereticos et schismaticos baptismum non habere, sine baptismo tamen receptis, cum peccata eorum tam inmania tamque sacrilega super eos esse crederent, eis tamen communicare quam separari ab unitate -maluerunt dicente Cypriano: neminem neminem aut a iure communionis aliquem si diuersum senserit amouentes.
passages.english: For although they believed that heretics and schismatics do not have baptism, yet when these had been received without baptism, and though they believed that their sins, so monstrous and so sacrilegious, were upon them, they nevertheless preferred to be in communion with them rather than to be separated from unity, as Cyprian says: "judging no one, nor removing anyone from the right of communion if he has thought differently."
passages.notes: The quotation appears corrupt: "neminem neminem" is evidently a dittography, and a word such as "iudicantes" seems to have dropped out; translated on that assumption.

passages.original: tempore illo, quo dominus priora delicta recentibus poenarum exemplis cauenda monstrauit et idolum fabricatum adque adoratum est et propheticus liber ira regis contemptoris iucensus et schisma temptatum, idololatria gladio punita est, exustio libri bellica caede et peregrina captiuitate, schisma hiatu terrae, sepultis auctoribus uiuis et ceteris caelesti igne consumptis. quis iam dubitauerit hoc esse sceleratius commissum quod est grauius uindicatum? a talibus sacrilegis uenientes sine baptismo ut dicitis Cyprianum non contaminabant: quomodo uos contaminare poterant non conuicti sed conficti traditores? qui non si libros incendendos tradidissent, sed eos ipsi suis manibus incendissent, minoris fuissent utique sceleris quam si schisma committerent, quia illud mitius, illud grauius uindicatum est non humano arbitrio, sed diuino iudicio.
passages.english: At that time, when the Lord showed by fresh examples of punishment that former offences were to be guarded against, and an idol was made and worshipped, and the prophetic book was burned by the anger of a contemptuous king, and schism was attempted, idolatry was punished by the sword, the burning of the book by slaughter in war and captivity in a foreign land, schism by the opening of the earth, the authors being buried alive and the rest consumed by fire from heaven. Who now would doubt that the crime more heavily punished was the more wicked one committed? Those coming from such sacrilegious men without baptism, as you say, did not contaminate Cyprian: how could traitors who were not convicted but fabricated contaminate you? Even if they had not handed over the books to be burned, but had burned them themselves with their own hands, they would surely have been guilty of a lesser crime than if they committed schism, because the one was punished more mildly, the other more heavily, not by human choice but by divine judgment.
passages.notes: "iucensus" read as "incensus" (burned). "Traitors" renders traditores, those accused of handing over the scriptures in persecution. The sentence "qui non si..." is awkward in the Latin; the sense seems to be "even if they had not merely handed over the books...".

passages.original: quam consuetudinem — credo ex apostolica traditione uenientem, sicut multa non inueniuntur in litteris eorum neque in conciliis posterorum et tamen, quia per uniuersam custodiuntur ecclesiam, non nisi ab ipsis tradita et conmendata creduntur — hanc ergo saluberrimam consuetudinem per Agrippinum prodecessorem suum dicit sanctus Cyprianus quasi coepisse corrigi; sed sicut diligentius inquisita ueritas docuit, quae post magnos dubitationis fluctus ad plenarii concilii confirmationem perducta est, uerius creditur per Agrippinum corrumpi coepisse, non corrigi.
passages.english: This custom (coming, I believe, from apostolic tradition, just as many things are not found in their writings nor in the councils of later men, and yet, because they are kept throughout the whole church, are believed to have been handed down and commended by none other than them), this most wholesome custom, then, holy Cyprian says began, as it were, to be corrected by Agrippinus his predecessor; but, as the truth more carefully investigated has taught, which after great waves of doubt was brought to the confirmation of a plenary council, it is more truly believed to have begun to be corrupted by Agrippinus, not corrected.

passages.original: Ecclesia quippe catholica temporibus beati Cypriani et ante ipsum praeterito tempore aut rebaptizatos aut baptismum non habentes unitatis gremio continebat: aut illi aut illi salutem non nisi unitatis ipsius merito consecuti sunt. si enim non habebant baptismum qui ab haereticis ueniebant, sicut asserit Cyprianus, non recte admittebantur; et tamen eisdem ipse indulgentiam de domini misericordia propter unitatem ecclesiae non desperauit. ita ergo, si habebant baptismum, non recte rebaptizabantur. quid itaque illos nisi eadem unitatis caritas adiuuabat, ut, quod in sacramento tractando latebat humanam infirmitatem, diuina misericordia non reputaret amantibus pacem?
passages.english: For the Catholic church in the times of blessed Cyprian and in the time before him held in the bosom of unity either the rebaptized or those without baptism: either the one group or the other attained salvation only through the merit of that unity. For if those who came from the heretics did not have baptism, as Cyprian asserts, they were not rightly admitted; and yet he himself did not despair of pardon for them from the Lord's mercy on account of the unity of the church. So, likewise, if they had baptism, they were not rightly rebaptized. What, then, helped them but the same charity of unity, so that what in the handling of the sacrament was hidden from human weakness, divine mercy would not reckon against those who loved peace?

passages.original: quos in Africa infamauerunt et in transmarino iudicio non conuicerunt, se ab orbis terrarum communione separarunt, cum etiam si uera crimina obicerent multo sunt maiora scelera haeresum et schismatum. unde sine baptismo sicut sensit ipse uenientes et in catholicam communionem non per baptismum recepti non potuerunt maculare Cyprianum. neque in eo ipso, in quo se dicunt imitari Cyprianum, inueniunt quid respondeant de - recepto baptismo Maximianistarum cum eis, quos ex eo numero, quos concilio suo plenario damnatos etiam terrenarum potestatum iudicio persecuti (sunt), in suam communionem in eodem ipso episcopatu in quo damnauerant reuocauerunt.
passages.english: [these men], [on account of] those whom they defamed in Africa and did not convict in the judgment overseas, separated themselves from the communion of the whole world, when, even if they were bringing true charges, the crimes of heresies and schisms are much greater. Hence those coming without baptism, as he himself thought, and received into Catholic communion not through baptism, could not stain Cyprian. Nor, in that very point in which they say they imitate Cyprian, do they find what to answer concerning the accepted baptism of the Maximianists, together with those whom, from the number of those condemned in their plenary council and even pursued by the judgment of earthly powers, they recalled into their communion in the very same episcopal office in which they had condemned them.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence, continuing "on account of the name of traitors" from the preceding context. The final clause is syntactically confused in the Latin ("cum eis, quos ex eo numero, quos..."); translated by sense.

passages.original: Nunc ergo nos manentes in exemplo Cypriani consideremus etiam concilium Cypriani. quid ait Cyprianus? Audistis, inquit, collegae dilectissimi, quid mihi lubaianus coepi. scopus noster scripserit consulens mediocritatem nostram de inlicito et profano haereticorum baptismo quidque ego ei rescripserim, censens scilicet quod semel adque iterum et saepe censuimus haereticos ad ecclesiam uenientes ecclesiae baptismo baptizari et sanctificari oportere. item lectae sunt uobis et aliae Iubaiani litterae quibus pro sua sincera et religiosa dcuotione ad epistulam nostram rescribens non tantum consensit, sed et instructum se esse gratias egit.
passages.english: Now, then, abiding by the example of Cyprian, let us consider also the council of Cyprian. What does Cyprian say? "You have heard, most beloved colleagues," he says, "what Jubaianus our fellow bishop wrote to me, consulting my humble self about the unlawful and profane baptism of heretics, and what I wrote back to him, judging, namely, as we have judged once and again and often, that heretics coming to the church ought to be baptized and sanctified with the baptism of the church. Likewise other letters of Jubaianus have been read to you, in which, replying to our letter out of his sincere and religious devotion, he not only agreed but also gave thanks that he had been instructed."
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "lubaianus coepi. scopus" to Iubaianus coepiscopus, "dcuotione" to devotione.

passages.original: recitatae sunt enim, sicut in exordio commemoratum est. et nobis ergo recitentur, ut nos. quoque inde, quid sentiri oporteat, quantum dominus adiuuat indagemus. dicit forsitan quispiam: quid ergo? tu modo discis quid ad Iubaianum scripserit Cyprianus?\' iam legi, fateor, et profecto issem in eandem sententiam, nisi me ad diligentiorem considerationem reuocaret tanta auctoritas aliorum, quos uel pares gratia doctrinae uel etiam fortasse doctiores per tot gentes Latinas Graecas barbaras et ipsam Hebraeam ecclesia toto orbe diffusa parere potuit, quae ipsum quoque pepererat, qui mihi nullo modo uideri potuerunt frustra noluisse istam tenere sententiam, non quia fieri non potuit ut in obscurissima quaestione uerius pluribus unus pauciue sentirent, sed quia non facile pro uno uel paucis aduersus innumerabiles eiusdem religionis et unitatis uiros et magno ingenio et uberi doctrina praeditos nisi pertractatis pro uiribus adque perspectis rebus ferenda sententia est.
passages.english: For they were read out, as was mentioned at the beginning. So let them be read out to us too, so that we also may investigate from them, as far as the Lord helps, what ought to be thought. Perhaps someone says: What then? Are you only now learning what Cyprian wrote to Jubaianus? I have read it already, I confess, and I would certainly have gone over to the same opinion, had not the great authority of others called me back to more careful consideration, [men] equal in the grace of learning or perhaps even more learned, whom the Church spread through the whole world could bring forth among so many nations, Latin, Greek, barbarian and Hebrew itself, the Church which had also brought forth him [Cyprian]; and these could in no way seem to me to have refused to hold that opinion without reason, not because it could not happen that in a most obscure question one or a few should judge more truly than many, but because judgement should not lightly be given for one or a few against innumerable men of the same religion and unity, endowed with great talent and rich learning, unless the matters have been thoroughly treated and examined as far as one's strength allows.

passages.original: Si quis autem quaerit, quid interim teneam dum ista pertracto, respondeo primum mihi Cypriani litteras suggessisse quod teneam, donec perspiciam quale sit quod coepit postea disputari. ait quippe ipse Cyprianus: sed dicit aliquis: quid ergo fiet de his qui in praeteritum de haeresi uenientes ad ecclesiam sine baptismo admissi sunt? utrum isti reuera sine baptismo fuerint an ideo sint admissi, quia illi qui admittebant eos habere baptismum intellegebant, mox considerabimus. uerumtamen quae soleret esse ecclesiae consuetudo, satis idem Cyprianus ostendit, qui ait in praeteritum de haeresi ad ecclesiam uenientes sine baptismo admissos.
passages.english: But if anyone asks what I hold in the meantime while I examine these matters, I answer that, first, the letters of Cyprian have suggested to me what I should hold, until I see clearly what sort of thing it is that afterwards began to be disputed. For Cyprian himself says: "But someone says: what then will become of those who in the past, coming from heresy to the church, were admitted without baptism?" Whether these were in fact without baptism, or were admitted because those who admitted them understood that they had baptism, we shall consider shortly. Nevertheless, what the custom of the church used to be, the same Cyprian shows clearly enough when he says that in the past those coming from heresy to the church were admitted without baptism.

passages.original: Scribit ergo ad Iubaianum Cyprianus de haereticorum baptismo, qui uidentur ei foris positi et extra ecclesiam constituti uindicare sibi rem nec iuris sui nec potestatis: quod nos, inquit, nec ratum possumus nec legitimum putare, quando hoc aput eos esse constet inlicitum. nec nos abnuimus, cum qui aput haereticos uel in aliquo schismate extra communionem ecclesiae baptizatur, non ei prodesse in quantum haereticorum et schismaticorum peruersitati consentit, nec illos qui baptizant, quamuis ipsum et uerum dent baptismi sacramentum, recte tamen facere extra ecclesiam colligere et contra ecclesiam sentire.
passages.english: Cyprian writes, then, to Jubaianus about the baptism of heretics, who, placed outside and established outside the church, seem to him to claim for themselves a thing that is neither within their right nor their power: "which," he says, "we can consider neither valid nor legitimate, since it is evident that this is unlawful among them." Nor do we deny that when someone is baptized among heretics or in some schism outside the communion of the church, it does not profit him insofar as he consents to the perversity of the heretics and schismatics; nor [do we deny] that those who baptize, although they give the very and true sacrament of baptism, nevertheless do not act rightly in gathering outside the church and thinking against the church.

passages.original: Recte autem non mouit Cyprianum, quod scripsit Iubaianus Nouatianenses rebaptizare eos qui ad se ex catholica uenirent. neque enim quidquid haeretici peruerse fuerint imitati propterea faciendum a catholicis non est, quia illi simi- Uter faciunt;
passages.english: Rightly, however, Cyprian was not moved by what Jubaianus wrote, that the Novatianists rebaptize those who come to them from the Catholic [church]. For it is not the case that whatever heretics have perversely imitated must therefore not be done by Catholics, because they do something similar;
passages.notes: "simi- Uter" read as "similiter".

passages.original: Ideo autem non se nouam aut repentinam rem statuisse beatus Cyprianus ostendit, quia sub Agrippino fieri iam coeperat. anni sunt, inquit, multi et longa aetas ex quo sub Agrippino bonae memoriae uiro conuenientes episcopi plurimi hoc statuerunt. proinde ab ipso Agrippino res noua facta est. quomodo autem dicat: adque exinde in hodiernum tot milia haereticorum in prouinciis nostris ad ecclesiam conuersi non aspernati sunt neque cunctati.
passages.english: Now the blessed Cyprian shows that he had not laid down a new or sudden thing, because it had already begun to be done under Agrippinus. "Many years," he says, "and a long age have passed since, under Agrippinus, a man of good memory, a great many bishops meeting together laid this down." Accordingly the new thing was introduced by Agrippinus himself. But how he can say, "and from then until today so many thousands of heretics in our provinces, converted to the church, have not scorned or hesitated,"
passages.notes: The sentence beginning 'quomodo autem dicat' continues into the following passage ('...non uideo', 'I do not see'), so it is left incomplete here.

passages.original: aqua enim ecclesiae fidelis et salutaris et sancta est bene utentibus, ea uero bene uti extra ecclesiam nemo potest. male utentibus autem et foris et intus ad supplicium geritur, non ad praemium suffragatur. et ideo baptismus corrumpi et adulterari non potest, etsi a corruptis et adulteris habeatur, sicut et ipsa ecclesia incorrupta et casta et pudica est, et ideo non ad eam pertinent auari raptores faeneratores, quos non tantum foris sed etiam intus esse multis litterarum suarum locis Cyprianus ipse testatur, et tamen non mutato corde baptizantur et baptizant.
passages.english: For the water of the church is faithful and saving and holy for those who use it well, but no one can use it well outside the church. For those who use it badly, however, both outside and inside, it is administered to their punishment and does not avail them toward reward. And therefore baptism cannot be corrupted or adulterated, even if it is held by the corrupt and adulterous, just as the church itself is also uncorrupted and chaste and modest. And therefore the greedy, robbers and usurers do not belong to it, whom Cyprian himself testifies in many places of his letters to be not only outside but also inside; and yet, with unchanged heart, they are baptized and they baptize.

passages.original: et deo quidem, aput quem sunt praesentia quae uentura sunt, etiam quod futuri sunt iam sunt, nos autem secundum id quod in praesenti est quisque hominum quaerimus, utrum in illius ecclesiae membris, quae unica columba dicta est et sponsa Christi sine macula et ruga, hodie deputandi sint de quibus dicit Cyprianus in epistula quam commemoraui, quod uiam domini non tenerent nec data sibi ad salutem caelestia mandata seruarent, quod non facerent domini uoluntatem patrimonio et lucro studentes, superbiam sectantes, aemulationi et dissensioni uacantes, simplicitatis et fidei neglegentes, saeculo uerbis solis et non factis renuntiantes, unusquisque sibi placentes et omnibus displicentes. quodsi eos in suis membris nec illa columba cognoscit et talibus, si in eadem peruersitate permanserint, dicturus est dominus: non noui uos;
passages.english: And to God indeed, with whom things that are to come are present, even what they will be they already are; but we ask, according to what each man is at present, whether those ought today to be counted among the members of that church which is called the one dove and the bride of Christ without spot or wrinkle, of whom Cyprian says in the letter I have mentioned that they did not keep the way of the Lord, nor observe the heavenly commandments given them for salvation; that they did not do the Lord's will, being intent on property and gain, pursuing pride, given over to rivalry and dissension, neglectful of simplicity and faith, renouncing the world in words alone and not in deeds, each pleasing himself and displeasing everyone. But if not even that dove recognizes them among her members, and to such, if they persist in the same perversity, the Lord will say: "I do not know you;
passages.notes: The sentence continues into the following passage.

passages.original: sed illa consuetudo, quam etiam tunc homines sursum uersus respicientes non uidebant a posterioribus institutam, recte ab apostolis tradita creditur, et talia multa sunt, quae longum est repetere. quapropter si non nihil dicebant, quibus id quod ei uisum est uolens persuadere Cyprianus ait: nec quisquam dicat: \'quod accepimus ab apostolis hoc sequimur\', quanto robustius nunc dicimus: \'quod ecclesiae consuetudo semper tenuit et quod haec disputatio dissuadere non potuit et quod plenarium concilium confirmauit, hoc sequimur\'! huc accedit, quia bene perspectis ex utroque latere disputationis rationibus et scripturarum testimoniis potest etiam dici: \'quod ueritas declarauit, hoc sequimur.\'
passages.english: But that custom, which even then men looking back toward earlier times did not see to have been instituted by later men, is rightly believed to have been handed down by the apostles; and there are many such things, which it would be long to recount. Therefore, if those were saying something, to whom Cyprian, wishing to persuade them of what seemed right to him, says, "Let no one say, 'We follow what we received from the apostles,'" how much more strongly do we now say: "What the custom of the church has always held, and what this argument could not dissuade from, and what a plenary council has confirmed, this we follow!" Add to this that, once the reasonings of the argument on both sides and the testimonies of the Scriptures have been well examined, it can also be said: "What the truth has declared, this we follow."

passages.original: Nam reuera illud, quod quidam Cypriani disputationibus opponebant, quod ait apostolus: uerumtamen omni modo siue per occasionem siue per ueritatem Christus adnuntietur, recte Cyprianus refellit ostendens ad causam haereticorum non pertinere, quoniam de his dicebat apostolus, qui cum maliuola inuidia sua quaerentes interius uersabantur. Christum quidem adnuntiabant, sicut se habet ueritas qua Christo credimus, sed non eo animo quo a bonis euangelistis illius columbae filiis adnuntiabatur.
passages.english: For indeed, that which some opposed to Cyprian's arguments, what the apostle says, "Nevertheless in every way, whether by pretext or in truth, let Christ be proclaimed," Cyprian rightly refutes, showing that it does not pertain to the case of heretics, since the apostle was speaking of those who, seeking their own ends with malevolent envy, were moving about inside [the church]. They proclaimed Christ indeed, as the truth stands by which we believe in Christ, but not in the spirit in which he was proclaimed by the good evangelists, the children of that dove.

passages.original: Sed tamen quia inuidia diaboli mors intrauit in orbem terrarum et imitantur illum qui sunt ex parte ipsius, non per illud quod a deo creati sunt, sed per illud quod a se ipsis peruersi sunt, sicut commemorat ipse Cyprianus, quia et diabolus antequam esset diabolus angelus fuit et bonus fuit, unde. sunt in unitate Christi qui sunt ex parte diaboli? procul dubio, sicut ipse dominus ait, inimicus homo hoc fecit, qui superseminauit zizania. sicut ergo et intus quod diaboli est arguendum est, sic et foris quod Christi est agnoscendum est.
passages.english: But nevertheless, since through the envy of the devil death entered into the world, and those who are of his party imitate him, not by that in which they were created by God, but by that in which they were perverted by themselves, as Cyprian himself mentions, since the devil too, before he was the devil, was an angel and was good, whence then are there in the unity of Christ those who are of the devil's party? Without doubt, as the Lord himself says, "An enemy has done this," who sowed tares over [the wheat]. Just as, therefore, what is the devil's must be rebuked even inside, so too what is Christ's must be acknowledged even outside.
passages.notes: 'unde.' read as 'unde' introducing the question; the stop appears to be misplaced.

passages.original: tales tamen etiam intus et accipiunt baptismum et habent et tradunt sanctum per se ipsum nec ulla ex parte illorum malignitate uiolatur, in qua in finem usque perdurant. quocirca idem nos beatus Cyprianus docet per se ipsum esse considerandum baptismum uerbis euangelicis, sicut accepit ecclesia, consecratum, non adiuncta neque permixta ulla peruersitate adque malitia siue accipientium siue tradentium, quandoquidem ipse utrumque nos ammonet, et intus fuisse quosdam non seruantes beniuolam caritatem, sed in inuidia et maliuola dissensione uersatos, de quibus Paulus apostolus locutus est, et ex parte diaboli esse inuidos, sicut in epistula quam de zelo et liuore scripsit apertissima uoce testatur.
passages.english: Yet such men, even inside, both receive baptism and hold and hand it on, holy in itself, and it is in no part violated by their malice, in which they persist to the end. Wherefore the same blessed Cyprian teaches us that baptism is to be considered in itself, consecrated by the words of the Gospel as the church received it, with no perversity and malice of either those receiving or those conferring it joined or mingled with it; since he himself reminds us of both things: that there were some inside who did not keep kindly charity but were given over to envy and malevolent dissension, of whom the apostle Paul spoke; and that the envious are of the devil's party, as he testifies in the plainest terms in the letter he wrote on jealousy and envy.

passages.original: Quid quod etiam mirum est, quod accidere posse inuenit qui diligenter aduertit, quosdam salua caritate docere aliquid inutile, sicut Petrus gentes iudaizare cogebat, sicut ipse Cyprianus haereticos denuo baptizari — unde talibus bonis membris in caritate radicatis et in aliquo non recte ingredientibus dicit apostolus: si quid aliter sapitis, id quoque deus uobis reuelabit —, et quosdam rursus sine caritate docere aliquid salubre, de qualibus dominus ait: cathedram Moysi sedent. quae dicunt facite, quae autem faciunt facere nolite. dicunt enim et non faciunt. unde et apostolus de illis inuidis et maliuolis, christianam tamen salutem adnuntiantibus: siue occasione, inquit, siue ueritate Christus adnuntietur. quapropter et intus et foris peruersitas hominum corrigenda est, diuina uero sacramenta et eloquia non hominibus tribuenda.
passages.english: What of this, which is indeed remarkable, which one who pays careful attention finds can happen: that some, with charity intact, teach something unprofitable, as Peter compelled the Gentiles to live as Jews, as Cyprian himself [compelled] heretics to be baptized again — whence to such good members, rooted in charity and in some matter not walking rightly, the apostle says, "If in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal this also to you" — and that others again, without charity, teach something wholesome, of whom the Lord says: "They sit on the seat of Moses. What they say, do; but what they do, do not do. For they say and do not do." Whence also the apostle says of those envious and malevolent men who nevertheless proclaimed Christian salvation: "Whether by pretext or in truth, let Christ be proclaimed." Therefore the perversity of men must be corrected both inside and outside, but the divine sacraments and utterances are not to be attributed to men.

passages.original: et tamen eos intus fuisse significauit cum ait: quomodo dicunt quidam in uobis quia resurrectio mortuorum non est? auaros autem ubi non detestatur? aut uero potuit quicquam dici uehementius, quam ut idolorum seruitus auaritia diceretur, sicut idem apostolus posuit nec Cyprianus aliter intellexit et litteris suis ubi opus erat inseruit? qui tamen confitetur temporibus suis in ecclesia fuisse non qualescumque auaros, sed raptores et faeneratores, nec quoslibet homines, sed episcopos. quamquam et istos, de quibus ait apostolus: sermo eorum sicut cancer serpit, uellem intellegere foris fuisse; sed me Cyprianus ipse non sinit. cum enim ad Antonianum scribens ostenderet ante tempus ultimae separationis iustorum et iniquorum nullo modo esse propter commixtionem malorum ab unitate ecclesiae recedendum, ubi declarat quam sit sanctus et illa quam meruit martyrii claritate dignissimus, ait: quantus arrogantiae tumor est, quanta humilitatis et lenitatis obliuio et arrogantiae suae quanta iactatio, ut quis audeat aut facere posse se credat, quod nec apostolis concessit dominus, ut zizania a frumento putet se posse discernere aut, quasi ipsi palam ferre et aream purgare concessum sit, paleas conetura tritico separare, cumque apostolus dicat: \'in domo autem magna non solum uasa aurea sunt et argentea, sed et lignea et fictilia\', (aurea et argentea uasa uideatur eligere, lignea uero et fictilia) contemnere et abicere et damnare, quando non nisi in die domini uasa lignea diuini ardoris incendio concrementur et fictilia ab eo cui data est ferrea uirga frangantur.
passages.english: And yet he indicated that they were inside when he said: "How do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?" And where does he not abhor the greedy? Or indeed could anything be said more vehemently than that greed should be called idolatry, as the same apostle put it, and Cyprian understood it no differently and inserted it in his letters where needed? Yet he confesses that in his own times there were in the church not just any greedy men, but robbers and usurers, and not just any men, but bishops. And I would wish to understand those too, of whom the apostle says, "Their speech spreads like a cancer," to have been outside; but Cyprian himself does not allow me. For when, writing to Antonianus, he was showing that before the time of the final separation of the just and the unjust one must by no means withdraw from the unity of the church on account of the admixture of the wicked, where he declares how holy he is and how most worthy of that glory of martyrdom which he earned, he says: "How great is the swelling of arrogance, how great the forgetfulness of humility and gentleness, and how great the boasting of one's arrogance, that anyone should dare or believe he can do what the Lord did not grant even to the apostles: that he should think he can distinguish the tares from the wheat, or, as if it were granted to him to carry the fan and clean the threshing floor, should try to separate the chaff from the wheat; and when the apostle says, 'But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware,' he should seem to pick out the vessels of gold and silver, but despise, cast away and condemn the wooden and earthenware ones, when only on the day of the Lord will the wooden vessels be burned up by the fire of the divine blaze and the earthenware ones be broken by him to whom the iron rod has been given."
passages.notes: 'palam' read as 'palam' = 'palam' (fan, i.e. winnowing shovel; 'palam ferre'); 'conetura' read as 'conetur a'. The bracketed words in the quotation are the edition's supplement.

passages.original: neque nos dicimus: \'ubicumque et quomodocumque baptizati gratiam baptismi consequuntur,\' si gratia baptismi in ipsa salute intellegitur quae per sacramenti celebrationem confertur, sed hanc salutem multi nec intus consequuntur, quamuis sacramentum quod per se sanctum est eos habere manifestum sit. recte itaque nos dominus ammonet in euangelio, ne consentiamus male suadentibus et sub Christi nomine ambulantibus, sed hi et intus et foris inueniuntur, quia nec foras exeunt nisi prius intus mali fuerint, et utique de uasis in domo magna positis dicebat apostolus: si quis autem emundauerit semet ipsum ab istiusmodi, erit uas in honore sanctificatum, utile domino, ad omne opus bonum semper paratum. quomodo autem se ab eiusmodi quisque mundare debeat, paulo superius ostendit dicens: recedat ab iniquitate omnis qui nominat nomen domini, ne audiat in fine cum palea, siue quae ante de area uolauit siue quae in ultimo separanda est: recedite a me qui operamini iniquitatem. unde apparet quidem, sicut dicit Cyprianus, non ea statim suscipienda et adsumenda quae iactantur in Christi nomine, sed quae geruntur in Christi ueritate. sed non utique in Christi ueritate geritur fundos insidiosis fraudibus rapere, usuris multiplicantibus faenus augere, saeculo uerbis solis renuntiare. quae omnia etiam intus geri satis idoneus testis ipse declarat.
passages.english: Nor do we say, "Wherever and however they are baptized, they obtain the grace of baptism," if the grace of baptism is understood as that very salvation which is conferred through the celebration of the sacrament; but many do not obtain this salvation even inside, although it is evident that they have the sacrament, which is holy in itself. Rightly, then, does the Lord warn us in the Gospel not to consent to those who counsel evil and walk under Christ's name; but these are found both inside and outside, since they do not go outside unless they were first evil inside. And certainly it was of the vessels set in the great house that the apostle said: "If anyone cleanses himself from such, he will be a vessel for honour, sanctified, useful to the Lord, always ready for every good work." And how each one ought to cleanse himself from such, he showed a little above, saying: "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity," lest he hear at the end, with the chaff, whether that which flew off the threshing floor beforehand or that which is to be separated at the last: "Depart from me, you who work iniquity." Whence it indeed appears, as Cyprian says, that what is to be received and accepted is not at once whatever is boasted in Christ's name, but what is done in Christ's truth. But it is certainly not done in Christ's truth to seize estates by treacherous frauds, to increase gain by multiplying interest, to renounce the world in words alone. And that all these things are done even inside, he himself, a sufficiently competent witness, declares.

passages.original: et tamen, inquit, neque hoc baptisma haeretico prodest, si quamuis Christum confessus extra ecclesiam fuerit occisus. hoc uerissimum est. extra ecclesiam quippe occisus caritatem non habuisse conuincitur, de qua apostolus dicit: et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest. quodsi propter hoc quia caritas deest passio nihil prodest, nec illis prodest, quos intus in inuidia et maliuolentia sine caritate uiuere Paulus dicit, Cyprianus exponit, et tamen uerum baptisma possunt et accipere et tradere. salus extra ecclesiam non est. quis negat? et ideo quaecumque ipsius ecclesiae habentur, extra ecclesiam non ualent ad salutem. sed aliud est non habere, aliud non utiliter habere.
passages.english: "And yet," he says, "not even this baptism benefits a heretic, if, though he has confessed Christ, he has been killed outside the Church." This is most true. For one killed outside the Church is proven not to have had charity, of which the apostle says: "And if I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have charity, it profits me nothing." But if suffering profits nothing because charity is lacking, neither does it profit those who, as Paul says and Cyprian explains, live inside [the Church] in envy and malice without charity; and yet they can both receive and confer true baptism. There is no salvation outside the Church. Who denies it? And therefore whatever things belonging to the Church itself are held outside the Church do not avail for salvation. But it is one thing not to have, another not to have profitably.

passages.original: Ecclesiae catholicae consuetudinem pristinam nunc teneri, cum ab haereticis uel schismaticis uenientes, si euangelicis uerbis consecratum baptismum perceperunt, denuo non baptizantur, beato Cypriano teste utimur. ipse quippe sibi quaestionem proposuit ex ore utique fratrum siue quaerentium ueritatem siue pro ueritate certantium. inter disputationes enim suas, quibus uolebat ostendere denuo baptizandos haereticos, de quibus satis pro tempore libris superioribus disseruimus, ait: sed dicit aliquis: quid ergo fiet de his qui in praeteritum de haeresi ad ecclesiam uenientes sine baptismo admissi sunt?
passages.english: That the ancient custom of the Catholic Church is now kept, when those coming from heretics or schismatics, if they have received baptism consecrated with the words of the Gospel, are not baptized again, we use the blessed Cyprian as witness. For he himself put the question to himself, doubtless from the mouths of brothers, whether seeking the truth or contending for the truth. For among his arguments, by which he wished to show that heretics should be baptized again, which we have discussed sufficiently for the present in the previous books, he says: "But someone says: What then will become of those who in the past, coming from heresy to the Church, were admitted without baptism?"

passages.original: porro si uerum est aput haereticos et schismaticos non esse baptismum Christi, quanto minus obessent in unitate positis aliena peccata, si ad unitatem uenientibus et sine baptismo admissis soluerentur et propria! nam si teste Cypriano unitatis uinculum tantum ualet, quomodo possent laedi peccatis alienis qui nollent ab unitate recedere, si etiam non baptizati peccatis propriis non perirent, qui ad eam uellent ex haeresi accedere?
passages.english: Furthermore, if it is true that the baptism of Christ does not exist among heretics and schismatics, how much less would the sins of others harm those placed in unity, if even their own sins were loosed for those coming to unity and admitted without baptism! For if, as Cyprian testifies, the bond of unity has such power, how could those who would not withdraw from unity be harmed by the sins of others, if even those who wished to come to it from heresy did not perish by their own sins although not baptized?

passages.original: Quod autem adiungit Cyprianus et dicit: non tamen quia aliquando erratum est, ideo semper errandum est, cum magis sapientibus et deum timentibus congruat patefactae et perspectae ueritati libenter adque incunctanter obsequi quam pertinaciter adque obstinate contra fratres et consacerdotes\' pro haereticis reluctari, uerissime dicit, nec alteri potius quam sibi aduersatur qui resistit apertissimae ueritati. sed per illa quae tam multa iam diximus, quantum arbitror, liquido apparet et certum est baptismum Christi nec haereticorum peruersitate, cum aput eos datur et sumitur, posse uiolari.
passages.english: But what Cyprian adds, saying: "Yet because there was once an error, it does not follow that one must always err, since it befits the wise and those who fear God rather to obey the truth, once disclosed and perceived, willingly and without hesitation, than stubbornly and obstinately to struggle against brothers and fellow priests on behalf of heretics," he says most truly; and he who resists the most evident truth opposes no one so much as himself. But through the many things we have already said, as I think, it plainly appears and is certain that the baptism of Christ cannot be violated even by the perversity of heretics, when it is given and received among them.
passages.notes: A stray mark after "consacerdotes" in the source has been ignored.

passages.original: quod nullo modo eligerent fieri, nisi amplius sibi aduersari arbitrarentur horrorem hominum de iterata tinctione quam considerationem de perdita defensione. quod non ideo dixerim, quia humano sensu deterreri debuimus, si ab haereticis uenientes denuo baptizari ueritas cogeret, sed quia sanctus Cyprianus ait hoc ipso magis haereticos ad necessitatem ueniendi adigi potuisse, si rursus in catholica baptizarentur, propterea commemorare uolui, quantus paene in omnium mentibus huius facti horror insidat, quem diuinitus infusum esse crediderim, ut aduersus quaslibet disputationes quas infirmi discutere nequeunt horrore ipso ecclesia muniretur.
passages.english: which they would by no means have chosen to happen, unless they thought that people's horror at a repeated dipping was more against them than consideration of the position they had lost. I would not have said this because we ought to have been deterred by human feeling, if the truth compelled that those coming from heretics be baptized again; but because holy Cyprian says that heretics could have been driven all the more by this very thing to the necessity of coming, if they were baptized again in the Catholic [Church], I therefore wished to mention how great a horror at this act is lodged in the minds of almost everyone, which I would believe was infused by God, so that the Church might be fortified by that very horror against any arguments which the weak are unable to refute.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the subject (the Donatists of Primian's party) is supplied by the preceding context.

passages.original: Quaero itaque, si baptismo Iohannis peccata dimittebantur, quid amplius praestari potuit per baptismum Christi eis, quos apostolus Paulus post Iohannis baptismum Christi baptismo uoluit baptizari? si autem Iohannis baptismo non dimittebantur peccata, utrumnam meliores erant Iohanne Cypriani temporibus, de quibus ipse dicit quod fundos insidiosis fraudibus rapiebant et usuris multiplicantibus faenus augebant, quibus tamen baptizantibus fiebat remissio peccatorum P an quia eos unitas ecclesiae tenebat? quid ergo?
passages.english: I ask therefore: if sins were forgiven by the baptism of John, what more could be granted through the baptism of Christ to those whom the apostle Paul wished to be baptized with the baptism of Christ after the baptism of John? But if sins were not forgiven by the baptism of John, were those in Cyprian's time better than John, those of whom he himself says that they seized estates by treacherous frauds and increased their gain by multiplying usury, and yet when they baptized, remission of sins took place? Or was it because the unity of the Church held them? What then?
passages.notes: "P" before "an" is a scanning error, probably for a question mark; omitted.

passages.original: Non itaque idcirco haereticus ius baptismi optinere potuit quia prior baptizauit, sed quia non suo baptismo baptizauit, et si ius baptizandi non habuit, tamen Christi est quod dedit et ille Christi est quod accepit. multa enim contra ius dantur nec tamen ideo uel nulla uel non data dicuntur. neque enim et ille, qui saeculo uerbis solis et non factis renuntiat, iure accipit baptismum et tamen accipit. nam tales in ecclesia et Cyprianus suis temporibus fuisse commemorat et nos experimur et gemimus.
passages.english: Therefore the heretic could not obtain the right of baptism because he baptized first, but because he did not baptize with his own baptism; and even if he did not have the right of baptizing, still what he gave is Christ's and what that man received is Christ's. For many things are given against right, and yet they are not for that reason said to be either nothing or not given. For neither does the one who renounces the world with words alone and not deeds receive baptism rightfully, and yet he receives it. For Cyprian too records that such people were in the Church in his times, and we experience it and groan.
passages.notes: The opening sense is compressed: Augustine seems to argue that the heretic's baptism is valid not because he baptized first but because it was not his own (but Christ's).

passages.original: cum ergo et intus sint mortui neque latentes — nam non de illis tanta diceret Cyprianus —, qui uel non pertineant ad illam uiuam columbam uel nondum pertineant, et foris sint mortui qui manifestius ad eam uel non pertineant uel nondum pertineant, uerumque sit non posse ab eo uiuificari alterum qui ipse non uiuit, manifestum est eos, qui intus a talibus baptizantur, si uera conuersione cordis accedunt, ab eo uiuificari cuius est baptismus, si autem saeculo uerbis et non factis renuntiant, quales Cyprianus et intus esse testatur, nec ipsos uiuificari nisi conuertantur et uerum tamen habere baptismum, etiamsi non conuertantur; unde etiam exteriores mortuos, quamuis neque uiuant neque uiuificent, habere tamen baptismum uiuum qui eis tunc prosit ad uitam, si conuertantur ad pacem, similiter manifestum est.
passages.english: Since, therefore, there are dead people both inside, and not hidden ones (for Cyprian would not say so much about those), who either do not belong or do not yet belong to that living dove, and there are dead people outside, who more manifestly either do not belong or do not yet belong to her, and it is true that another cannot be given life by one who does not himself live, it is manifest that those who are baptized inside by such people, if they come with true conversion of heart, are given life by him whose baptism it is; but if they renounce the world with words and not deeds, such as Cyprian testifies are inside too, they themselves are not given life unless they are converted, and yet they have true baptism, even if they are not converted; whence it is similarly manifest that the dead outside also, although they neither live nor give life, nevertheless have a living baptism, which will then benefit them for life if they are converted to peace.

passages.original: Non itaque de sola consuetudine, sed etiam de ueritatis ratione praesumit, qui nullorum hominum peruersitate peruersum fieri dicit sacramentum dei quod etiam in peruersis esse declaratur. certe Iohannes apostolus apertissime dicit: qui odit fratrem suum, in tenebris est usque adhuc, et iterum: qui odit fratrem suum homicida est. cur ergo tales intus baptizant, quos in maliuola inuidia fuisse Cyprianus ipse commemorat?
passages.english: Therefore it is not from custom alone, but also from the reasoning of truth, that he takes his stand who says that the sacrament of God, which is declared to exist even in the perverse, is not made perverse by the perversity of any people. Certainly the apostle John says most plainly: "He who hates his brother is in darkness even until now," and again: "He who hates his brother is a murderer." Why then do such people baptize inside [the Church], who Cyprian himself records were in malicious envy?

passages.original: si enim de his qui in nos peccauerant dictum est: si non dimiseritis peccata hominibus, nec pater uester dimittet uobis peccata uestra, quanto magis fieri non potest ut eis peccata dimittantur, qui fratres a quibus diliguntur oderunt et in ipso odio baptizantur, quibus tamen postea correctis non rursum baptismus datur, sed ipsa uenia quam tunc accipere non meruerunt in uera conuersione praestatur! ideoque etiam illa, quae ad Quintum scripsit Cyprianus, et illa, quae cum collegis suis Liberali Caldonio Iunio et ceteris ad Saturninum Maximum et alios, bene considerata nullo modo proferenda sunt aduersus totius ecclesiae catholicae consensionem, cuius se illi membra esse gaudebant et unde se neque ipsi praeciderunt neque diuersa sentientes praecidi passi sunt, donec aliquando in domini uoluntate per plenarium concilium licet post multos annos quid esset rectius eluceret non aliqua nouitate instituta, sed antiquitate roborata.
passages.english: For if it was said concerning those who had sinned against us: "If you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive you your sins," how much more impossible is it that sins be forgiven to those who hate the brothers by whom they are loved, and are baptized in that very hatred; and yet, when they are afterwards corrected, baptism is not given to them again, but the very pardon which they did not then deserve to receive is granted in true conversion! And therefore both what Cyprian wrote to Quintus, and what he wrote with his colleagues Liberalis, Caldonius, Junius and the others to Saturninus, Maximus and others, when well considered, should by no means be brought forward against the consensus of the whole Catholic Church, whose members they rejoiced to be, and from which they neither cut themselves off nor allowed those who thought differently to be cut off, until at some time, by the Lord's will, through a plenary council, though after many years, what was more correct should shine forth, not by some novelty instituted, but by antiquity confirmed.
passages.notes: "peccauerant" (had sinned) may reflect a variant; sense unaffected.

passages.original: Ad Pompeium etiam scripsit Cyprianus de hac eadem re, ubi aperte indicat Stephanum, quem Romanae ecclesiae episcopum tunc fuisse didicimus, non solum sibi ad ista non consensisse, uerum etiam contra scripsisse adque praecepisse. qui utique Stephanus non propterea communicauit haereticis, quia baptisma Christi, quod in eorum peruersitate integrum mansisse cognouit, inprobare non ausus est. nam si non habent baptismum qui de deo praua sentiunt, hoc posse et intus accidere iam satis ut arbitror disputatum est.
passages.english: Cyprian also wrote to Pompeius on this same matter, where he openly indicates that Stephen, who we have learned was then bishop of the Roman church, not only did not agree with him on these points, but even wrote and gave instructions to the contrary. This Stephen certainly did not on that account hold communion with heretics, because he did not dare to disapprove the baptism of Christ, which he recognized had remained intact in their perversity. For if those who think wrongly about God do not have baptism, that this can also happen within [the Church] has already, I think, been sufficiently argued.

passages.original: Et quod in Canticis canticorum ecclesia sic describitur: hortus conclusus, soror mea sponsa, fons signatus, puteusaquae uiuae, paradisus cum fructu pomorum, hoc intellegere non audeo nisi in sanctis et iustis, non in auaris et fraudatoribus et raptoribus et faeneratoribus et ebriosis et inuidis, quos tamen cum iustis baptismum habuisse commune, cum quibus communem non habebant utique caritatem, ex ipsius Cypriani litteris, sicut saepe commemoraui, uberius discimus et docemus. nam dicat mihi aliquis, quomodo inrepserint in hortum conclusum et fontem signatum, quos saeculo uerbis solis et non factis renuntiasse Cyprianus et tamen intus fuisse testatur. si enim et ipsi ibi sunt, et ipsi sponsa Christi sunt. itane uero talis est illa sine macula et ruga, et illa speciosa columba tali membrorum parte turpatur? an istae sunt spinae, in quarum medio est illa sicut lilium, quod in eodem cantico dicitur?
passages.english: And as for the Church being described thus in the Song of Songs: "A garden enclosed, my sister, my bride, a fountain sealed, a well of living water, a paradise with the fruit of apples", I do not dare to understand this except of the holy and the just, not of the greedy and the fraudulent and robbers and usurers and drunkards and the envious, who nevertheless had baptism in common with the just, though they certainly did not have charity in common with them, as we learn and teach more fully from the letters of Cyprian himself, as I have often mentioned. For let someone tell me how they crept into the enclosed garden and the sealed fountain, those who, as Cyprian testifies, renounced the world in words only and not in deeds, and yet were within. For if they too are there, they too are the bride of Christ. Is she, then, who is without spot or wrinkle, really such, and is that beautiful dove defiled by such a part of her members? Or are these the thorns, in the midst of which she is like a lily, as is said in the same Song?
passages.notes: "puteusaquae" read as "puteus aquae".

passages.original: aut quomodo salui fiunt per aquam, qui sancto baptismate male utentes, cum uideantur esse intus, usque in finem uitae in flagitiosis et perditis moribus perseuerant? aut quomodo non sunt per aquam saluati, quos in praeteritum cum eo baptismate, quod in haeresi acceperant, in ecclesiam simpliciter admissos Cyprianus ipse commemorat? eadem quippe arcae unitas eos saluos fecit in qua nemo nisi per aquam saluatus est. ipse enim dicit: potens est dominus misericordia sua indulgentiam dare et eos qui ad ecclesiam simpliciter admissi in ecclesia dormieruntab ecclesiae suae muneribus non separare. si non per aquam, quomodo in arca? si non in arca, quomodo in ecclesia? si autem in ecclesia, utique in arca, et si in arca, utique per aquam.
passages.english: Or how are they saved through water who, misusing holy baptism, though they seem to be within, persevere to the end of life in shameful and depraved conduct? Or how were they not saved through water whom Cyprian himself mentions as having been admitted into the Church in the past simply, with the baptism they had received in heresy? For it was the same unity of the ark that saved them, in which no one was saved except through water. For he himself says: "The Lord is able by his mercy to grant pardon, and not to separate from the gifts of his Church those who, admitted simply to the Church, have fallen asleep in the Church." If not through water, how in the ark? If not in the ark, how in the Church? But if in the Church, then certainly in the ark; and if in the ark, then certainly through water.
passages.notes: "dormieruntab" read as "dormierunt ab".

passages.original: Ad haec respondeo, quoniam quisquis etiam intus confitetur se deum nosse, factis autem negat — quales sunt auari et inuidi et qui propter fraternum odium non meo, sed sancti Iohannis apostoli testimonio dicuntur homicidae —, et spem non habent, quia malam conscientiam gerunt, et perfidi sunt, quia non id agunt quod deo uouerunt, et mendaces, quia falsa profitentur, et daemoniaci, quia diabolo et angelis eius in suo corde praebent locum, et uerba eorum putredinem operantur, cum corrumpunt mores bonos per conloquia mala, et infideles sunt, quoniam quod deus talibus minatur inrident, et scelerati quia nefarie uiuunt, et antichristi, quia mores eorum Christe aduersantur, et a deo maledicti, quia ubique tales sancta scriptura execratur, et mortui, quia carent uita iustitiae, et inpacati, quia contrariis factis cum dei sermone confligunt, et blasphemi, quia per eorum perditos actus nomini christiano derogatur, et profani, quia ab illo dei sanctuario spiritaliter interiore seclusi sunt, et sacrilegi, quia in se ipsis templum dei male uiuendo corrumpunt, et antistites diaboli, quia fraudi et auaritiae quae est idololatria seruiunt. tales autem nonnullos; immo plurimos et apostolus Paulus et episcopus Cyprianus etiam intus esse testantur. cur ergo isti baptizant? cur etiam quidam, qui saeculo uerbis et non factis renuntiant, et ab huiusmodi moribus non mutati baptizantur et quando mutantur non rebaptizantur? iam uero quod indignatur et dicit: ecce ad qualia cogitur, ecclesia consentire et.
passages.english: To this I reply that whoever, even within, confesses that he knows God but denies him by his deeds — such as are the greedy and the envious and those who, on account of hatred of a brother, are called murderers, not on my testimony but on that of the holy apostle John — such people both have no hope, because they bear a bad conscience; and are faithless, because they do not do what they vowed to God; and liars, because they profess falsehoods; and possessed, because they give place in their heart to the devil and his angels; and their words work corruption, since they corrupt good morals by evil conversations; and they are unbelievers, since they mock what God threatens against such people; and wicked, because they live impiously; and antichrists, because their conduct opposes Christ; and cursed by God, because holy Scripture everywhere execrates such people; and dead, because they lack the life of righteousness; and without peace, because by contrary deeds they fight against the word of God; and blasphemers, because through their depraved acts the Christian name is disparaged; and profane, because they are shut out spiritually from that inner sanctuary of God; and sacrilegious, because by living wickedly they corrupt the temple of God in themselves; and priests of the devil, because they serve fraud and greed, which is idolatry. Yet both the apostle Paul and the bishop Cyprian testify that some — indeed very many — such people are even within. Why then do these baptize? Why too are some who renounce the world in words and not in deeds baptized without being changed from such conduct, and when they are changed are not rebaptized? And now, as to his indignation when he says: "See to what sort of things the Church is forced to consent, and
passages.notes: The passage breaks off mid-quotation; it continues in the following context. "Christe" read as "Christo".

passages.original: aut si non nasci* tur ex spiritu nisi qui ueraci conuersione mutatur, omnes qui saeculo uerbis et non factis renuntiant non utique de spiritu, sed ex aqua sola nascuntur, qui tamen et intus teste Cypriano sunt. necesse est enim ut unum de duobus concedatur: aut illi qui fallaciter saeculo renuntiant nascuntur de spiritu, quamuis ad perniciem, non ad salutem, adque ita possunt et haeretici, aut si illud, quod scriptum est: sanctus enim spiritus disciplinae effugiet fictum, etiam ad hoc ualet, ut fallaciter saeculo renuntiantes non nascantur de spiritu, potest quis baptizari aqua et non nasci de spiritu et frustra Nemesianus ait: neque spiritus sine aqua operari potest nec aqua sine spiritu.
passages.english: Or if no one is born of the Spirit except one who is changed by true conversion, then all who renounce the world in words and not in deeds are certainly not born of the Spirit, but of water alone; and yet, on Cyprian's testimony, they are within. For one of two things must be conceded: either those who renounce the world deceitfully are born of the Spirit, though to their ruin, not to their salvation, and so heretics can be too; or, if what is written, "For the holy Spirit of discipline will flee from deceit", also holds to the effect that those who deceitfully renounce the world are not born of the Spirit, then someone can be baptized with water and not be born of the Spirit, and Nemesianus says in vain: "Neither can the Spirit work without water, nor water without the Spirit."
passages.notes: "nasci* tur" read as "nascitur".

passages.original: si autem n ö n dimiseritis hominibus, neque pater uester dimittet uobis. hinc et Iohannes ait: quia caritas cooperit multitudinem peccatorum, quam utique non habebant illi ac per hoc super harenam aedificabant, de quibus idem Cyprianus dicit quod intus in maliuola inuidia etiam temporibus apostolicis sine caritate conuersabantur. et ideo intus quidem esse uidebantur, sed foris erant, quia in illa petra per quam significatur ecclesia non erant.
passages.english: "But if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive you." Hence John too says that "charity covers a multitude of sins"; which charity those people certainly did not have, and therefore were building on sand, of whom the same Cyprian says that, within, they lived in malevolent envy without charity even in apostolic times. And therefore they seemed indeed to be within, but they were outside, because they were not on that rock by which the Church is signified.
passages.notes: The saying "charity covers a multitude of sins" is from 1 Peter, though attributed here to John.

passages.original: si uero a deo non est, quomodo gratiam dei aut habere aut conferre alicui potest?\' sed sicut ista eodem modo dicta manifestissime falsa sunt, sic etiam illa, quae ut conuincerentur haec dicta sunt. baptizant enim maliuoli et inuidi, sicut concedit ipse Cyprianus, quia eos etiam intus esse testatur. sic ergo possunt etiam haeretici baptizare, quia baptismus sacramentum Christi est, inuidia uero et haeresis opera diaboli, quae quisquis habuerit non hinc efficit ut, si habet sacramentum Christi, etiam ipsum numeretur inter.
passages.english: "But if it is not from God, how can it either have the grace of God or confer it on anyone?" But just as these things, said in the same way, are most manifestly false, so too are those things which these were said to refute. For the malevolent and envious do baptize, as Cyprian himself concedes, since he testifies that they too are within. So therefore heretics too can baptize, because baptism is a sacrament of Christ, while envy and heresy are works of the devil; and whoever has these does not thereby bring it about, if he has the sacrament of Christ, that the sacrament itself is counted among
passages.notes: The sentence breaks off; the context continues "the works of the devil".

passages.original: beatum dixerunt populum cui haec sunt: beatus populus cuius est dominus deus ipsius. si ergo isti sunt filii alieni qui in rebus temporalibus et abundantia terrenae felicitatis beatitudinem ponunt et diuina praecepta contemnunt, uideamus si non idem ipsi sunt de quibus Cyprianus ita dicit, in se quoque transfigurans eos, ut de his se dicere ostendat cum quibus sacramenta communicabat: dum uiam domini, inquit, non tenemus nec data nobis ad salutem caelestia mandata seruamus. fecit dominus noster uoluntatem patris, et nos non facimus domini uoluntatem patrimonio et lucro studentes, superb i a m sectantes et cetera. at si isti baptismum et habere et tradere poterant, cur negatur esse posse in filiis alienis?
passages.english: they called the people blessed who have these things: "Blessed is the people whose God is the Lord." If then these are the alien sons who place blessedness in temporal things and the abundance of earthly prosperity, and despise the divine commandments, let us see whether they are not the very ones of whom Cyprian speaks thus, transferring them onto himself too, so as to show that he is speaking of those with whom he shared the sacraments: "While we do not keep to the way of the Lord," he says, "nor observe the heavenly commandments given to us for salvation. Our Lord did the will of the Father, and we do not do the will of the Lord, devoted to property and gain, pursuing pride" and so on. But if these could both have and hand on baptism, why is it denied that it can exist among alien sons?
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the opening clause is incomplete.

passages.original: cum uero illa consuetudo et a ueritate propagata et ueritate roborata repperiatur, nihil in hac sententia pertimescimus. et tamen si illi circa fratres inuidi erant et maligni aut circa deum ingrati, ecce qualibus communicabant, ecce quales diuersa sentientes, sicut Cyprianus praedixit, a iure communionis non amouebant, ecce a quibus non polluebantur in conseruatione unitatis, ecce quantum amandum sit uinculum pacis, ecce quid considerent qui nobis de praecessorum episcoporum concilio calumniantur, quorum caritatem non imitantur et quorum exemplo considerato iure damnantur.
passages.english: But since that custom is found to have been both handed down from the truth and strengthened by the truth, we fear nothing in this statement. And yet, if those men were envious and malicious toward their brothers or ungrateful toward God, see with what sort of people they held communion; see what sort of people, though holding different views, they did not, as Cyprian declared, remove from the right of communion; see by whom they were not polluted in preserving unity; see how much the bond of peace is to be loved; see what they should consider who slander us about the council of earlier bishops, whose charity they do not imitate and by whose example, when it is considered, they are justly condemned.

passages.original: sed numquid, quia salutaris non est extraneis, ideo ipsa non est? aqua enim diluuii constitutis intra arcam salutaris fuit, extra arcam uero mortifera fuit; eadem tamen fuit. et multi extranei id est inuidi, quos ex parte diaboli esse Cyprianus dicit et de scripturis ostendit, uelut intus uidentur, et tamen nisi essent extra arcam non morerentur per aquam. tales enim baptismus cum eo male utuntur necat, sicut illis de quibus dicit apostolus bonus odor Christi erat in mortem. cur ergo non suscipiunt aliquid caeleste uel schismatici uel haeretici, sicut spinae seu zizania pluuiam, sicut ipsi qui extra arcam fuerunt aquam de cataractis caeli uenientem susceperunt quidem, sed ad perniciem, non ad salutem?
passages.english: But surely, because it is not saving to outsiders, it does not therefore not exist? For the water of the flood was saving to those placed within the ark, but deadly outside the ark; yet it was the same water. And many outsiders, that is the envious, whom Cyprian says are of the devil's party and shows this from the Scriptures, seem as it were to be within; and yet, unless they were outside the ark, they would not die through the water. For baptism kills such people when they misuse it, just as to those of whom the apostle speaks the good odour of Christ was unto death. Why then do neither schismatics nor heretics receive something heavenly, as thorns or tares receive the rain, as those very people who were outside the ark did indeed receive the water coming from the cataracts of heaven, but to their ruin, not to their salvation?
passages.notes: The sentence beginning "Why then do neither..." reads as a rhetorical question meaning "Why should they not receive...".

passages.original: iustitia enim et iniquitas duae et diuersae res sunt. si iniqui 20 habent baptisma, iusti non habent; si autem iusti habent, iniqui habere non possunt. dubium autem non est iustos solos baptismum Christi possidere qui soli possideant et gratiam Christi et ueritatem\\ hoc certe falsum est illis quoque fatentibus. et illi quippe inuidi qui sunt ex parte diaboli et intus positi, 25 sicut dicit Cyprianus, adque apostolo Paulo notissimi baptismum habebant nec ad membra illius columbae quae in petra tuta est pertinebant.
passages.english: For justice and iniquity are two different things. If the unjust have baptism, the just do not have it; but if the just have it, the unjust cannot have it. Now there is no doubt that the just alone possess the baptism of Christ, since they alone possess both the grace of Christ and the truth. This is certainly false, as even they themselves admit. For indeed those envious men too, who are of the devil's party and yet placed within, as Cyprian says, and very well known to the apostle Paul, had baptism, and did not belong to the members of that dove which is safe in the rock.
passages.notes: The numbers 20 and 25 are line numbers from the printed edition and have been omitted. The sentence 'Now there is no doubt that the just alone possess…' appears to be the end of the hypothetical objector's speech (begun in the preceding context), and 'This is certainly false' is Augustine's reply. The double backslash in the text likely marks where the quotation ends.

passages.original: Huic respondemus: Immo magis mirandum est et magna laude praedicandum, quod tantum isti dilexerint unitatem, ut, quos praeuaricatores ueritatis arbitrabantur, cum eis in unitate perseuerantes ab eis pollui non timerent. nam cum iste dixisset: illud mirandum est quod quidam nostri praeuaricatores ueritatis haereticis suffragantur et christianis aduersantur, uidebatur esse dicturus: \'propterea decernimus eis non esse communicandum.\' non hoc dixit, sed ait: propterea decernimus haereticos baptizandos esse, seruans quod pacificus Cyprianus ante praestruxerat dicens: neminem iudicantes aut a iure communionis aliquem si diuersum senserit amouentes. cum ergo Donatistae nobis calumniantur et nos dicunt traditores, si quis existat uel Iudaeus uel paganus, qui lecto isto concilio et nos et ipsos secundum eorum regulas unitatis appellet praeuaricatores, uelim scire ad hoc tam graue crimen refutandum adque diluendum quomodo nobis agenda sit causa communis.
passages.english: To him we reply: On the contrary, it is rather to be wondered at and proclaimed with great praise that these men loved unity so much that they did not fear being polluted by those whom they considered betrayers of the truth, while persevering in unity with them. For when this man had said, "What is to be wondered at is that some of our own, betrayers of the truth, support heretics and oppose Christians," he seemed about to say, "Therefore we decree that we must not hold communion with them." He did not say this, but said, "Therefore we decree that heretics must be baptized," keeping to what the peace-loving Cyprian had laid down beforehand, saying, "judging no one, nor removing anyone from the right of communion if he has thought differently." So, since the Donatists slander us and call us traditors, if some Jew or pagan should come forward who, having read this council, should call both us and them betrayers according to their rules of unity, I would like to know how we are to plead our common cause in order to refute and wash away so grave a charge.
passages.notes: "Traditors" (traditores): those who handed over the Scriptures during persecution. "Betrayers" renders praevaricatores.

passages.original: aput auaros numquid est deus? et tamen est baptismus. ita et aput haereticos. aput quos enim est deus templum dei sunt. quae autem compositio templo dei cum idolis? porro auaritiam idololatriam Paulus sentit, Cyprianus consentit, et idem ipse inter collegas raptores et tamen baptizatores cum magna tolerantiae mercede uersatur.
passages.english: Is God with the greedy? And yet baptism is [there]. So also with heretics. For those with whom God is are the temple of God. But what agreement has the temple of God with idols? Moreover, Paul holds that greed is idolatry, Cyprian agrees, and yet he himself lives among colleagues who are robbers and yet baptizers, with great reward for his forbearance.

passages.original: omnes ergo, id est et nos et ipsi, quia ex illa unitate propagati sumus, traditores sumus. sed nos duobus modis defendimur, quia et huic concilio ubi hoc pronuntiatum est non consentimus saluo iure unitatis, sicut Cyprianus ipse praedixit, et bonis malos in unitate catholica, donec in fine a tritico palea separetur, nihil obesse arbitramur. isti autem, quia et hoc concilium tamquam pro se proferunt et malorum communione quasi contagione bonos perire contendunt, non inueniunt, quomodo dicant aut priores christianos unde isti propagantur non fuisse traditores, quia isto conoilio conuincuntur, aut ad se non pertinere facinora priorum, quia nobis maiores nostros obiciunt.
passages.english: All of us, therefore, that is, both we and they, since we have been propagated from that unity, are traditors. But we are defended in two ways: both because we do not agree with this council where this was pronounced, while keeping the right of unity, as Cyprian himself foretold; and because we hold that the wicked do no harm to the good within catholic unity, until at the end the chaff is separated from the wheat. But they, since they both put forward this council as if on their own behalf and contend that the good perish through communion with the wicked as through contagion, cannot find a way to say either that the earlier Christians from whom they are propagated were not traditors, since they are convicted by this council, or that the crimes of their predecessors do not concern them, since they throw our forebears in our faces.
passages.notes: 'conoilio' read as 'concilio' (scanning error).

passages.original: et quando sanguinem suum uinum appellat de botruis adque acinisplurimisexpressumadque in unum coactum, gregem item nostrum significat commixtione adunatae multitudinis copulatum.haec uerba beati Cypriani indicant eum et intellexisse et dilexisse decorem domus dei, quam domum ex unanimis et concordibus constare adfirmauit et docuit testimonio prophetico et significatione sacramentorum; in qua utique non erant illi inuidi et sine caritate maliuoli, qui tamen baptizabant. ex quo apparet et in eis esse posse adque ab eis dari posse sacramentum Christi qui non sunt in ecclesia Christi, in qua non nisi unanimes et concordes habitare Cyprianus ipse testatur. neque enim saltem hoc dici potest tunc baptizare posse cum latent, quoniam illi Paulum apostolum non latebant quos in epistula sua ueracissimus testis notat et gaudere se dicit, quoniam et ipsi Christum adnuntiabant.
passages.english: "And when he calls his blood wine, pressed out of bunches and many grapes and brought together into one, he likewise signifies our flock joined by the mingling of a united multitude." These words of blessed Cyprian show that he both understood and loved the beauty of the house of God, which house he affirmed and taught, by prophetic testimony and by the meaning of the sacraments, consists of the like-minded and harmonious; in which certainly those envious and ill-willed men without charity were not, who nevertheless baptized. From this it appears that the sacrament of Christ can both be in, and be given by, those who are not in the Church of Christ, in which, as Cyprian himself testifies, none but the like-minded and harmonious dwell. Nor can it even be said that they can baptize only while they lie hidden, since those men were not hidden from the apostle Paul, whom that most truthful witness marks out in his letter, and he says he rejoices because they too were proclaiming Christ.
passages.notes: Run-together words (acinisplurimisexpressumadque) separated as 'acinis plurimis expressum adque'.
